newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish banks help push Madrid stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Spanish banks help push Madrid stocks higher.

text.p: A strong first-quarter performance by Spain's second-largest bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya helped push banking stocks and the overall Spanish market higher on Thursday, dealers said.
The Madrid bourse ended up 3.42 points, or 0.70 percent, to a record high of 490.71. The IBEX index of 35 leading shares ended up 41.27, or 0.74 percent, at 5,629.30.

BBV reported profits rose 24.8 percent in Q1, largely in line with expectations, although analysts pointed to unexpectedly strong trading profits and noted cautious provisioning was proof of the quality of the group's earnings.
"The market was trading in line with Europe. The banks, particularly Santander and Popular, did well as people are beginning to discount growth," a trader said.
Banks outpaced the market, with BBV closing up 100 pesetas, or 1.12 percent, at 9,010 off its daily peak of 9,070.

Santander took advantage of the benign outlook for banks, rising 90 pesetas or 0.91 percent, to 9,990, while Popular, whose first-quarter results are due next on April 23, gained 360, or 1.33 percent, to 4,356.
